sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - Marketplace FBA Store

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French and German legal tradition, with EU-derived administrative and financial regulatory overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: DTA Luxembourg-United States (Convention of 20 December 1996, as amended by Protocol of 2004 and 2009)
DTA Luxembourg-Hong Kong SAR (Agreement of 2 November 2007)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisional application)
EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement / Investment Protection Agreement (2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as amended by Law of 10 August 2015 on the modernisation of company law); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, including the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 5 July 2022); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 12 January 2019 on the practical operation of the RBE; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on anti-money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies (as amended); FATF Recommendations as transposed through EU Directives 2005/60/EC, 2015/849/EU, 2018/843/EU and 2018/1673/EU.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (Register of Beneficial Owners is not fully public post-CJEU judgment C-37/20; access is restricted to competent authorities and to persons demonstrating a legitimate interest under Luxembourg law of 26 December 2022; obliged entities retain enhanced-access rights under AML law)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif notarié) for the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Notaire, Ordre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Apostille Convention 1961; notarial deed is domestic, no apostille required for the deed itself, but all underlying foreign documents require apostille)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of the foreign corporate shareholder's constitutive documents, board resolutions and certificate of good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or competent authority of the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague countries (document-by-document chain of attestation)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies, proof of residential address and identity attestations of all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing state passport authority and municipal registry / bank-certified attestation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where government-issued) and notarial certification of copies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Personal or corporate bank reference letter evidencing source of funds for the minimum share capital (EUR 12,310) and future operational runway
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution in the EU/EEA or a reputable third-country bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or notarial certification; SWIFT/account-attestation standard applied by the notary and the CSSF-regulated banks

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filings with covered-entity annexes
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, approved intermediary, or the SARL through its registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not required; electronic lodgement via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorised signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN List (required for USD payment rails through Amazon Pay, Stripe, Airwallex), UK OFSI Consolidated List, and CSSF public warnings; PEP status determination mandatory per CSSF Regulation 12-02 article 2(3) and FATF Recommendations 12, 24 and 25; enhanced due diligence automatically applies to foreign PEPs, PEP family members and close associates; no incorporation is permitted if any screened party matches a sanctions designation or is the subject of a freezing measure under Luxembourg or EU law; ongoing transaction monitoring is required at the fintech/bank account-opening stage.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCSL (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) official online portal: https://www.lbr.lu; name availability search via RCSL electronic filing interface
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate legal names must be framed in French or German (practical standard: French), using the Latin alphabet; the legal-form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' is mandatory; hybrid foreign trade names must be transliterated into Latin script and may be accompanied by a Latin-script equivalent; ideographic or non-Latin names such as Chinese characters may only be used as an auxiliary translated name, never as the statutory RCSL name without a Latin transliteration; the name must be distinctive and may not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing RCSL-registered enterprise, European Economic Interest Grouping, or protected trademark registered in Luxembourg.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Crédit, Épargne, Caisse (requires CSSF authorisation as credit institution)
Assurance, Réassurance, Mutuelle, Prevoyance (requires CAA insurance-sector approval)
Fonds, SICAV, SICAF, OPC, FIS, RAIF, FCP (requires CSSF fund-sector authorisation or RAIF notification)
Bourse, Exchange, Stock Exchange, Trading Platform (misleading financial-market indication)
Luxembourg, Luxemburg, État, Administration nationale, Grand-Duché (requires prior ministerial authorisation where implying state sponsorship)
National, Federal, European, Euro, Union, BCE (terms suggesting official EU or government characteristics)
Avocat, Notaire, Huissier, Réviseur, Expert-Comptable, Audit (reserved to registered regulated professions)
Société Nationale, Chambre, Barreau (implying statutory public-law body status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation is valid for 60 days and may be renewed once by refiling through the LBR portal; if the RCSL rejects a name as unavailable, identical or confusingly similar, the applicant may (i) file a fresh reservation with distinguishing features or additional suffixes (e.g., geographic qualifier, registration number), (ii) send a written objection to the RCSL registrar within 15 days of the rejection notice citing prior-use evidence and trademark registrations, or (iii) within 3 months, file a legal appeal (recours en annulation) before the Tribunal administratif of Luxembourg where the rejection is based on public order or ministerial authorisation refusal; disputes concerning similarity to an existing registered name are ultimately adjudicated by the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg in commercial proceedings; attorneys' costs for a formal appeal typically range EUR 2,500-7,500 excluding court fees.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted subject to strict conditions: the registered office must be a genuine physical address in Luxembourg, and virtual/domiciliation services are lawful only when provided by a CSSF-licensed domiciliation agent governed by the Law of 31 May 1999, as amended; the agent must maintain actual premises, receive correspondence in Luxembourg, keep a nominal-shareholder and UBO transparency file, and provide substance attestations; a pure mailbox or offshore-managed virtual address without local substance is non-compliant and will trigger RBE and tax-substance review; for an Amazon FBA e-commerce SARL, domiciliation with an approved agent is routinely accepted provided the company maintains Luxembourg bank accounts, board records and substance documentation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 15% annual probability for a low-risk, non-licensed e-commerce FBA SARL with a CSSF-registered domiciliation agent and clean AML profile); probability materially increases to 40-55% if the company uses non-regulated virtual office configurations, has a PEP as UBO, processes high-risk payment flows, or receives tax-authority scrutiny under the Luxembourg substance rules and EU ATAD case law.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search, availability certificate and 60-day name reservation via LBR/RCSL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR published statutory tariff; approximately EUR 38 per reservation filing plus handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (constitution of the SARL) with minimum share capital attestation and articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Ordre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial fee schedule (tarif notarial), generally EUR 500-750 excluding VAT for a standard cash-corporate deed, plus disbursements; market range EUR 900-1,400 including drafting

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Fixed registration duty (droit d'enregistrement) on the notarial incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Article 153 of the Luxembourg Registration Duties Law; fixed duty EUR 75 per deed, plus notary handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL registration filing and judicial-seal formalities for the SARL (limited liability company, non-listed)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) via LBR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: RCSL/LBR fee schedule: EUR 24 registration filing fee plus statutory RESA publication charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation act and notices in the RESA official electronic compendium (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice - RESA official journal service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory official-journal tariff of approximately EUR 75-82 per insertion, charged per act; no court publication required for standard SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostilles and consular legalization of foreign corporate shareholder documents, UBO passport copies and good-standing certificates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the county of origin / consulates / Apostille competent authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention 1961 per-document fees EUR 20-40 (Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs and foreign counterparts); consular certification EUR 50-120 per document where no apostille regime applies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of the articles of association, incorporation resolutions and complete KYC/AML bundle into French or German
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn/certified translator in Luxembourg or notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Certified translation market rate EUR 35-60 per standard page plus notarial attestation; typical 6-8 pages for a SARL incorporation dossier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing with the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) via the notary or the company's registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RBE / LBR (electronic lodgement through notary or authorised professional intermediary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR published schedule: EUR 10 electronic filing fee plus professional handling charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, UBO and PEP piercing, AML/CFT risk assessments, corporate structural recommendations and approval of incorporation resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg avocat à la Cour (law firm)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg market benchmark of EUR 180-350 per hour; standard fixed-fee package for a low-risk single-UBO e-commerce SARL incorporation normally EUR 1,200-2,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial deposit for registered office/domiciliation service with a CSSF-licensed domiciliation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate: EUR 300-500 one-time setup fee plus EUR 100-200 monthly service for a standard SARL domiciliation and mail-forwarding arrangement; first-month fee included here

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (particularly the Law of 23 December 2016 modernising the SARL regime and the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS); Articles 710-1 to 710-26 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) and Articles 990-1 to 990-5 (general provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with electronic filing through the LPB (Luxembourg Public Business) e-registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) executed before a Luxembourg notary, followed by an application for registration and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed and fully paid-up capital of EUR 12,000 (cash or in-kind); cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) opened in the name of the company in formation at a Luxembourg credit institution, with the blocking certificate delivered to the notary prior to execution of the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST, that the notarial deed of incorporation of the Company, signed this day by the sole founding shareholder, is approved and adopted in its entirety. RESOLVED SECOND, that the Company's registered office is fixed at [registered address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and the right of the sole shareholder to transfer the registered office within the Grand Duchy is ratified. RESOLVED THIRD, that the share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed, issued and paid-up into the Company's blocked bank account, is ratified and the subscriber acknowledges the allocation of 100 registered shares. RESOLVED FOURTH, that [Full Name], [Nationality], is appointed as manager (gérant) of the Company for an unlimited term, with sole signature authority, full powers to register the Company with the Luxembourg Business Registers, and authority to open bank accounts and execute the Amazon FBA seller agreements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Articles of Association and Statutory Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg) in coordination with the filing counsel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a notary to draft the statutes under the Law of 10 August 1915 as amended, including corporate name, registered office address, corporate object limited to ISIC 4791 internet retail and related marketplace operations, capital structure, gérant powers, and duration. Verify name availability via a preliminary request to the RCS. Compile UBO (RBE) declarations and perform KYC/AML checks on the shareholder and manager.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (statuts)
Passport or national ID of each founding shareholder and appointed gérant
Proof of residential address of each shareholder and manager
Letter of intent / lease for the registered office address
UBO declaration under the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
Business plan and proof of source of funds for the EUR 12,000 capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is refused by the RCS for conflict or contravention of public policy, file a new name request with a distinct corporate denomination and re-execute the draft; any KYC deficiency is cured by supplementary ownership and source-of-wealth documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Blocked Capital Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, BGL BNP Paribas, Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État - Spuerkeess).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a pre-incorporation account in the name of 'LU_SARL in formation' with a Luxembourg bank. Deposit the full EUR 12,000 minimum capital and obtain a certificate of blocked deposit (attestation de blocage) issued by the bank to the notary, evidencing that the funds are irrevocably reserved for the company upon registration.
required_dossiers: Authenticated copies of passports of shareholders and gérant
Draft articles of association as provided by the notary
Proof of residential address and bank reference letter
UBO declaration and source-of-wealth questionnaire
Signed account mandate for the company in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC objections, submit a detailed source-of-funds letter and audited or tax-filed financial statements; if the account is rejected, open the blocked account with an alternative Luxembourg bank or apply to the notary to hold the funds in a notarial escrow account pending registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) in the district of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend before the notary for execution of the acte constitutif. The notary verifies the deposit certificate, confirms the gérant's power and integrity, reads the statutes, receives the signature of the founding shareholder, and issues certified copies (expéditions) and extracts for subsequent filings. The notary also files the AC registration form on the RCS electronic platform.
required_dossiers: Final draft articles of association
Bank certificate of blocked share capital deposit (attestation de blocage)
Identity documents of the signatories
Duly completed RCS registration form (formulaire A - inscription)
Declaration of non-refusal of the notary and consent of the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies an irregularity in the deposit certificate or identity documents, rectify by obtaining a corrected bank certificate or apostilled / legalised identity documents; if execution is postponed, re-schedule the notarial session without re-publication fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File electronically the notarial deed and registration application through the LBR e-desk portal. Pay the official inscription and publication fees. Upon admission, the company obtains its RCS number and is published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA); a legal entity legalisation certificate (extrait) is issued, granting legal personality.
required_dossiers: Original notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif)
RCS registration application form (formulaire A)
Proof of payment of registration and publication fees
Certified copy of the gérant's identity document and specimen signature
Extract of the criminal record or equivalent for the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises an admission incident (incident d'admission), the notary or client must supply the requested supplementary documents or corrections within one month; if the deadline is missed, re-file the application with a new fee payment and obtain a fresh notarial deed if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the AEDT via form 010 to obtain a national identification number, Luxembourg VAT number and, if cross-border B2C distance sales of imported goods are intended, register for the EU Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) and Union OSS scheme for intra-Community distance sales. Register as an employer with the CCSS when the first employee is hired. For Amazon FBA, submit the VAT ID and business registration evidence to the Amazon seller central account.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (extrait) evidencing registration
Articles of association (certified copy)
AEDT form 010 (business commencement declaration)
Proof of identity and residence of the gérant
Activity description for ISIC 4791 and estimated cross-border sales figures
Bank account details and establishment authorization application reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT application is queried for missing cross-border evidence, submit marketplace sales estimates and warehouse lease evidence; for IOSS registration delays, await AEDT confirmation and charge domestic VAT only until the OSS registration is active; any CCSS query is cured by providing the signed employment contracts and salary declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate General for Crafts, Trades and Commerce (Direction générale des classes moyennes), filed via the Guichet.lu single window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online application for the autorisation d'établissement under the amended Law of 2 September 2011, within six months of RCS registration and in any event before commencing retail activity. Demonstrate the professional qualification or delegation of a manager holding statutory Certificate of Professional Competence (or equivalent managerial experience), clean criminal record, and good repute.
required_dossiers: Application form completed on Guichet.lu
Extract from the RCS (not older than three months)
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of the gérant, or foreign equivalent
Proof of professional qualification or equivalent management experience (at least three years)
Proof of registered office and business premises
Declaration of no prior bankruptcy and solvency evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry requests additional proof of professional competence, submit the diploma equivalence or provide a statutory delegation to a qualified manager; if the authorization is refused, appeal to the administrative tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months or re-apply after curing the stated unlawfulness.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate General for Crafts, Trades and Commerce (Direction générale des classes moyennes), operating through the Guichet.lu e-government portal.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Establishment Authorization / Business License) issued under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA – Category D (Annex IV of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 May 2018): an internet retail and FBA fulfilment office/warehouse below the 20,000 m² warehouse threshold falls under the simplified registration/notification tier, requiring only an environmental notification form to the local commune administration; no scoping or full EIA report is mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharge to municipal sewer within the parameters of the Grand-Ducal Regulation on urban wastewater treatment implementing EU Directive 91/271/EEC (mandatory compliance with municipal pre-treatment limits, notably BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L and TSS ≤ 35 mg/L at the treatment plant); no direct VOC emissions from the FBA retail activity (only negligible off-gassing from packaged goods, below the 2 t/yr reporting threshold); packaging waste recovery and recycling obligations under EU Directive 94/62/EC and the Luxembourg packaging regulation, requiring a minimum 65% overall recycling rate by 31 December 2025 and registration with the national packaging compliance scheme (recycling body / eco-organisme).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: inspection and approval by the Luxembourg fire and rescue corps (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours – CGDIS) for any office/warehouse premises, including an emergency evacuation plan, fire alarm and extinguisher installation certificates (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued before occupation; structural load clearance: engineer's attestation for mezzanine shelving or racking in the fulfilment area confirming compliance with Luxembourg building codes (règlement des bâtisses); occupational clearance: workplace risk assessment (évaluation des risques) and health-and-safety registration with the ITM (Inspection du travail et des mines), plus a medical aptitude declaration for the applicable employees; if more than 15 employees are engaged, the employer must establish a mixed works council (comité mixte) and a safety delegate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority, for VAT matters; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Direct Tax Administration, for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) – Customs and Excise Administration, for customs, excise and import VAT; unified access portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu) and the AEDT e-space; official legal references: amended Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 and General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung, AO) of 22 May 1931.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – Incorporate the SARL by notarial deed and file the incorporation dossier with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) through MyGuichet.lu, obtaining the business identification number (matricule d'identification). Step 2 – File the initial VAT registration form (Form 214 / demande d'attribution d'un numéro de TVA) with the AEDT electronically via MyGuichet, citing the RCS matricule, registered office address, actual business activity code (ISIC 4791), expected annual turnover and the names of the natural person responsible for VAT; the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro de TVA, format 'LU' + 10 digits) normally within 10–15 business days. Step 3 – Request an EORI number from the Customs and Excise Administration (ADA) for import/export activities (format 'EO' + matricule); a Luxembourg EORI is a prerequisite for lodging export declarations and for operating under any inward/outward processing or customs warehousing procedure. Step 4 – Register for social security with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) for employer obligations; this is not a tax formality but is required for payroll compliance. Step 5 – Non-resident entrepreneurs (including non-resident shareholders acting as managers) must obtain a Luxembourg residential tax number (numéro d'identification, 13 digits) from the ACD for personal income tax and employer withholding registration; this number is also used for the municipal business tax file. Step 6 – File the annual VAT and CIT returns through the MyGuichet portal using the taxpayer's space; foreign sellers with no Luxembourg fixed establishment may alternatively use the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for distance sales and the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) for low-value consignments, but companies with an RCS-registered SARL in Luxembourg are treated as established and must register directly with the AEDT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – a Luxembourg SARL is a fully taxable resident company (société de capitaux) under Article 159 LIR; it is subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, 17% headline including the COVID solidarity surcharge of 7% on the base CIT) and to municipal business tax (taxe commerciale communale, rate varies by commune; in Luxembourg City approx. 6.75%, producing a combined statutory rate of roughly 24.94%); net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) applies at 0.5% generally, with a reduced 0.05% regime for qualifying asset holdings and an exemption threshold of EUR 500,000 for the 2024 assessment year; territorial scope: resident companies are taxable on worldwide income, with a foreign permanent establishment exemption available under Article 182(8) LIR only if the foreign PE income is subject to a comparable income tax in the source country; the SARL is not a pass-through entity – no partnership transparency whatsoever, and no tax transparency election exists under Luxembourg domestic law; the business scope (online marketplace FBA retail trading) is a fully taxable commercial activity with no special tax-incentive zone applicable to Luxembourg City.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate the US check-the-box regime, but the following elections are available: (i) fiscal unity / consolidation under Article 164bis LIR for corporate income tax and Article 164ter LIR for municipal business tax – a single group election may be made by a resident parent company holding at least 95% of the voting rights in one or more resident or EEA subsidiaries, submitted annually with the tax return; (ii) VAT grouping (assujettis uniques) under Article 60 of the VAT Law – by application to the AEDT, financially, economically and organisationally linked resident entities may form a single taxable person with one VAT number; (iii) PE exemption election under Article 182(8) LIR – the taxpayer may elect to exempt qualifying foreign permanent establishment profits instead of claiming tax credits; (iv) capital allowances elections under Articles 32 and 42bis LIR (declining-balance depreciation, investment tax credit of up to 15% for eligible digitalisation assets); (v) notional interest deduction election under Article 168bis LIR – an optional deduction on new equity capital (currently capped at 0.816% for 2024); (vi) the R&D super-deduction election (Article 57ter LIR) allows up to 100% additional deduction for R&D expenditures; (vii) hybrid mismatch elections are not available – Luxembourg implemented ATAD 2 via the Law of 21 December 2018, and the anti-hybrid rules automatically override any contrary contractual or statutory election; (viii) a 'self-employment option' is not applicable because SARL shareholders cannot be treated as self-employed for income tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA) pursuant to the amended Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, harmonized under Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EU-wide threshold applicable to intra-Community distance sales of goods: EUR 10,000 per calendar year (Article 357 VAT Directive; Article 58(vt) Luxembourg VAT Law) – if total distance sales from Luxembourg into other EU member states (including those deemed from Amazon FBA warehouses) remain below EUR 10,000, Luxembourg VAT at 17% applies; above the threshold, the seller must either register in each destination member state or use the OSS (non-Union/Union scheme). For purely domestic supplies from a Luxembourg-established SARL, there is no registration threshold – the company must be VAT registered from the day the first taxable transaction is performed; an optional small-business exemption (régime de la franchise) up to EUR 35,000 annual turnover may be applied but is not commercially viable for a marketplace FBA operator because it precludes input VAT deduction. Import VAT registration is required from the first import (no de minimis threshold) unless the IOSS scheme is used for consignments not exceeding EUR 150. Non-established foreign sellers stocking goods under Amazon FBA in a Luxembourg warehouse are registrable in Luxembourg regardless of the EUR 10,000 threshold because the place of supply of the onward sale is where the goods are located at the time of sale; Amazon's fulfilment services themselves are taxable B2B services located in the customer's jurisdiction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no general real-time fiscal clearance requirement, no digital tax stamping, and no mandatory B2B e-invoicing or API-based pre-clearance for commercial invoices. Mandatory structured electronic invoicing applies only to B2G transactions: since 18 March 2021, suppliers to the Luxembourg State and public-sector buyers must issue e-invoices through the PEPPOL network using the PEPPOL BIS 3.0, UBL (OASIS), or Factur-X formats; compliance is monitored by the Treasury (Trésorerie de l'État) and the Centre des technologies de l'information de l'État (CTIE). For B2B invoices, the VAT Law permits electronic invoicing provided the authenticity of origin and integrity of content are guaranteed through a qualified electronic signature, EDI, or a documented audit trail (Articles 92–93 of the VAT Law); paper invoices remain acceptable. The AEDT may require extraction in SAF-T LU format (audit-file standard) upon initiation of a tax audit; as of 2024 no live clearance API exists for VAT purposes. Operators using Amazon Seller Central are reminded that Amazon's marketplace seller portal issues invoices on behalf of the seller for EU supplies and provides the AEDT with seller data on request, which does not alter the seller's statutory obligation to maintain original commercial documentation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically delivered from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU customs territory qualify for zero-rating at 0% under Article 152-I-1° of the VAT Law provided: (i) the goods leave EU territory by means of transport of the seller or a third party acting on the seller's behalf within 90 days from dispatch (as a commercial reality rule; the law requires proof of exit, not a fixed 90-day customs deadline, but the AEDT applies the 90-day presumption); (ii) the seller holds the export declaration in its own name or in the name of an authorised customs representative; (iii) the seller retains in its books the transport contract, bill of lading/AWB/CMR and written purchase order identifying a non-EU buyer; and (iv) the export is made for the benefit of a non-EU purchaser or for a non-EU customer's account. For cross-border e-commerce: B2B services supplied to a non-EU established customer are zero-rated under the place-of-supply rule (Article 77(1) of the VAT Law); B2C digital services supplied to a non-EU consumer are also zero-rated; goods sold via Amazon FBA to EU consumers in other member states are NOT exported from Luxembourg and must be declared via OSS at the destination state's VAT rate; goods sold to a non-EU consumer (e.g., the UK after Brexit or the US) and physically exported directly from the Luxembourg logistics center qualify for zero-rating; if the goods are warehoused outside Luxembourg (e.g., an Amazon FBA centre in Germany) and then sold to a third-country customer, the export is zero-rated in the member state where the goods left the EU, and the Luxembourg seller must register there or use the OSS only within the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration lodged in the Luxembourg customs import/export system (MSIA-AI / EU AES) through the ADA, containing the EORI number, HS codes, declared commercial value and the unique Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit certificate (PDG – preuve de sortie) issued by the customs office at the EU border, or the AES post-departure message confirming exit with date of departure

Transport document: original Bill of Lading for sea freight, CMR waybill for road freight, Air Waybill for air freight, or international consignment note (rail/parcel), indicating the consignor (Luxembourg SARL), consignee (non-EU buyer) and destination outside the EU

Commercial invoice with the export declaration number, Incoterms 2020 rule (EXW, FOB, or DAP), the buyer's non-EU tax/VAT code, and a statement that goods are exported outside the EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103, bank confirmation, or Foreign Exchange Deal ticket) evidencing the receipt of foreign currency for the export sale in the seller's Luxembourg bank account
Amazon FBA shipment manifest (inventory transfer report, closure order, shipment event history) proving that the goods left the EU and matching the date of sale to the buyer
Freight forwarder's shipping instructions, packing list, and destination customs entry (import declaration from the destination country) as supplementary proof of actual arrival in the non-EU market
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT's export audit programme scrutinises the documentary chain for artificial fulfilment structures (especially Amazon FBA operations where the marketplace acts as seller of record for certain programmes). If the exporter cannot demonstrate (i) physical exit of goods, (ii) settlement of the invoice in foreign currency within a commercially reasonable period (the AEDT applies a 180-day presumption in export refund controls), or (iii) a genuine non-EU customer, the zero-rating is denied, input VAT previously deducted on related purchases is clawed back, and the VAT due is assessed at 17% with interest at the legal rate of 0.8% per quarter (Article 31(3) VAT Law), plus a late-payment penalty of 10% of the tax due (Article 25 amending Article 56 of the VAT Law). Where fictitious exporters claim refunds on the basis of forged transport documents, the criminal law applies: Article 396(2) of the General Tax Law provides fines of EUR 250 to EUR 250,000 for negligence or wilful misdeclaration; Article 397 AO provides for imprisonment of eight days to five years and/or fines of EUR 25,000 to EUR 250,000 for intentional tax fraud; in addition, the AEDT may revoke the exporter's EORI, require a bank guarantee up to 150% of the disputed amount, and reassess within a limitation period of five years (ten years in cases of fraud or concealment). The Luxembourg fiscal authorities cooperate with the EU Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) and the Amazon tax information sharing programme; the director of a Luxembourg SARL who signs a knowingly false export declaration bears personal criminal liability, while the company is jointly liable for the VAT clawback and fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the monetary authority, responsible for balance-of-payments reporting, prudential oversight of banks operating in Luxembourg, and EU TARGET2 settlement participation. Banking conduct and AML/CFT supervision is discharged by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). No separate Ministry of Finance exchange-control approval is required for current or capital transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible; Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls. Article 63 TFEU guarantees free movement of capital within the EU and with third countries, subject only to EU-wide sanctions screening. The capital account is fully open: equity injections, loans between affiliated undertakings, dividend distributions, and profit repatriation are unrestricted. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to tax clearance and reporting duties: (i) 15% domestic dividend withholding tax (5% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive with a 10% shareholding and 12-month holding period; 0% further where a Luxembourg participation-exemption regime applies), (ii) annual BCL direct-investment (EPURE) statistical declarations, and (iii) absence of any currency rationing, surrender, or prior authorization for e-commerce receipts. Current-account payments (Amazon FBA settlement remittances, supplier invoices, platform fees) are freely tradable and payable in EUR, USD, CNY, or any other freely usable currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirements exist for Luxembourg exporters. All Amazon marketplace receipts, marketplace payouts, and unrelated export proceeds may be held indefinitely in foreign currency without conversion. A Luxembourg SARL is free to convert 0% or 100% at its commercial discretion. Applicable obligations are limited to (i) banking record retention (Articles L. 100-116 of the Luxembourg Commercial Code), (ii) CSSF AML transaction scrutiny, and (iii) BCL quarterly direct-investment and external-asset/liability position reporting for cross-border settlements exceeding EUR 12,500 per single transaction in some statistical classes. No within-365-day mandatory repatriation or conversion timeline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Multi-Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Transaction Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and FX Hedging Line
Global Cash Management and Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High as auxiliary collection and FX conversion rails, Low as sole principal treasury bank. Stripe Payments Luxembourg S.à r.l. holds a CSSF-authorized electronic money institution (EMI) licence under PSD2 and can lawfully collect Amazon checkout payments, settle to the SARL, and maintain e-money balances; Airwallex operates EU-wide by passporting its Dutch (DNB) EMI licence, while Payoneer typically relies on partner banking arrangements. Legal constraints: an EMI may not grant credit or pay interest on e-money balances; funds are safeguarded, not deposit-guaranteed under the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme; and the SARL remains the sole obligor for commercial liabilities. Recommended structure is an EMI as a sub-collection gateway with weekly sweep sweeps to a BIL/Société Générale physical corporate account, thereby preserving full customer protection, FX price transparency, and CSSF end-client auditability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person or advanced video-identification onboarding is mandatory for all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of the SARL. Luxembourg Tier-1 banks will accept remote KYC for EU/EEA resident UBOs via regulated video-identity attestation, but for non-EU beneficial owners or shareholders with intermediate holding companies, a physical or videoconference interview with the client-facing compliance team in Luxembourg City is effectively required. A first signature specimen must typically be produced to the bank in hard copy or through a notarized signature act. Practical mandate: at least one managing director (natural person) must attend either (i) an in-person kick-off meeting at the bank's Luxembourg premises or (ii) a live CSSF-compliant video session, accompanied by a telecommunication-verification call from the account-opening team. Legalization, apostille, and sworn translation of passport, corporate articles, and UBO registry (RBE) extracts are required for any non-Luxembourg corporate shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU individual or holding-company shareholders with opaque source of wealth, especially 100% third-country ownership without a clear commercial track record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn statement of assets and source of funds signed by each UBO; audited financial statements or a bank reference letter from a top-50 global bank covering 12 months of transaction history; tax residence certificate; notarized and apostilled passport; certified copies of share register and constitutional documents; registered office certificate; reference from a Luxembourg certified fiduciary; and a MSB-relevant (multi-source business) narrative demonstrating that capitalization derives from verifiable e-commerce profit or divestiture proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border marketplace settlement fragmentation: simultaneous inflow streams from Amazon Seller Central (LU/US/DE), Stripe, and Airwallex with mismatched counterpart names in SWIFT messages.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Amazon Marketplace Services Agreement; Amazon Seller Central bank-account validation letter; three months of platform settlement reconciliation reports; a formal treasury policy designating the primary receiving bank account and authorized EMI pass-through accounts; and an independent accountant's agreement-to-reconcile letter detailing the matching of merchant ID, gross sales, fees, and payout currency to bank statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high frequency of international payments to China-based suppliers or FBA-warehouse inbound forwarding agents, triggering red flags for trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, purchase orders, customs declarations (SAD/EUCV), bills of lading, courier waybills (DHL/FedEx/Amazon Global Logistics), B2B marketplace order screenshots, and proof of delivery; supplier KYC file including business licence and bank account confirmation via SWIFT; and a recurring disbursement mandate locked in the bank's user rights matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO register (RBE) mismatch or delayed filing observed at bank's registry check, creating a presumption of inaccurate beneficial ownership disclosure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official RBE extraction filed within the legally prescribed 30-day window; notarial deed of incorporation; shareholder register ledger; bank-sanctioned UBO declaration form; and a clear organization chart showing ownership through Luxembourg, Belgium, or parent-company intermediate entities with full tax-exposure explanation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity contributions must be made by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR) to the designated capital escrow account, referencing purpose code 'CAPU' (Capital Increase) under SEPA, or SWIFT field 70/72 with explicit narrative 'APPORT EN CAPITAL — LU SARL — resolution dated [DD/MM/YYYY]'. The bank requires the legally effective notarized capital-increase deed, the Luxembourg RCS filing (eg. business reg. extract), and the UBO declaration before releasing funds. For intercompany loans, use purpose code 'FINC' (Financing) or 'INTC' (Intra-company payment) and a written loan agreement containing arm's-length interest and maturity to justify transfer-pricing treatment. All inbound funds must be reported under BCL EPURE classification codes in the monthly direct-investment return; a blocked account receiving a capital injection will be unblocked only after the bank has verified the deed and the corporate registry extract showing the registered capital increase, typically 3-7 business days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 (serial or cover) for cross-border supplier payments and platform fees, carrying proper purpose code 'TRAD' (trade) or 'GOODS' plus reference to the underlying invoice. For EU counterparties, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (minimum EUR 100k/day tier at BIL and Spuerkeess) provides TARGET2 real-time settlement. For large procurement of inventory destined to Amazon FBA centers, a commercial irrevocable documentary letter of credit (UCP600) issued by BIL or Société Générale Luxembourg, with two working-day bank-to-bank confirmation for Chinese beneficiary banks, is the recommended collateralized rail. Amazon Seller Central payouts are executed via Amazon's own treasury rail to the SARL's receiving account, typically settling in EUR (for DE/IT/ES/FR marketplaces) via SEPA, or USD via Fedwire/CHIPS through the local correspondent. The treasurer must maintain at least three clearing paths: (i) SWIFT for non-EU/USD/CNY invoices, (ii) SEPA-CT for Amazon disbursement concentration, and (iii) EMI orchestration for marketplace checkout funds, with automated daily zero-balancing sweeps to the primary account to avoid FX fragmentation and float leakage.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla OTC FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY deliverable CNH, EUR/GBP) with minimum 3-month commercial cover tenors, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Luxembourg credit institution and subject to CSSF initial-margin rules; eligible only against verified Amazon settlement forecasts and supplier invoices.
Rolling FX forwards (flexible delivery dates) to match FBA settlement volatility without forcing daily fixing, provided each roll is documented with a new trade confirmation and BCL EPURE update.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for regulated onshore currencies (notably EUR/CNY for FTC-linked supplier contracts) where full deliverability is unavailable; underlying commercial exposure must be demonstrated at each roll date.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD coupon and exchange-of-principal) for matched-term financing of warehouse inventory or intercompany shareholder loans beyond 12 months, subject to the SARL's internal investment policy and MiFID II professional-client suitability classification.

FX option strategies (zero-cost collars or purchased vanilla EUR/USD/USD/CNY options) for protecting minimum conversion rates on Amazon USD-denominated marketplaces while retaining upside; purchased options require prior board approval, but do not trigger derivative-margin collateral if the premium is paid upfront and no residual credit exposure extends beyond the option premium.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss statement, notes) filed via the eCDF portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS/LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year entity: shareholders' approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July of the following year; for non-calendar fiscal year-end, filing due within 1 month of the annual general meeting held no later than 6 months after the financial year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered coercive daily fine (astreinte) for continued non-filing; formal notice from the Public Prosecutor's Office; repeated default for more than six consecutive months may trigger administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC), and net wealth tax (IFT) return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 June following the fiscal year-end; automatically extended to 30 September for calendar-year companies when prepared and filed by a registered Luxembourg tax adviser or chartered accountant under an active e-filing mandate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of up to EUR 5,000, default interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid taxes, ex officio assessment, and enforced collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 September of every calendar year regardless of ownership changes; any shareholding transfer altering UBO composition must additionally be reported within 30 days of the transfer becoming known.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines for the SARL range from EUR 500 to EUR 20,000 for missing, inaccurate, or incomplete UBO declarations; imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years may apply for intentional false declarations; formal reminders and referral to the public prosecutor for persistent non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent annual audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé is triggered when the SARL exceeds any two of the following three thresholds at the balance sheet date for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for public-interest entities, upon shareholder request representing at least 10% of share capital, or where consolidated group rules require it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 18 December 2015; IFRS is not mandatory for a non-listed solo SARL but may be applied voluntarily for statutory accounts if the legal conditions are met.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Luxembourg SARL must maintain an up-to-date register of beneficial owners and file an annual confirmation with the RBE by 1 September, even if no ownership change has occurred during the year. Any direct or indirect share transfer or change in effective ownership must be declared within 30 days of the change. The annual confirmation attests that the recorded UBO information remains accurate and complete.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for a small e-commerce SARL below thresholds; if statutory audit becomes mandatory, typical certified audit fee for a small Luxembourg company is $6,000 – $15,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17.7% (17% corporate income tax plus 7% solidarity surcharge)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP tax box regime exempts 80% of qualified IP income, yielding an effective corporate income tax rate around 5%; R&D tax credit of up to 20%; participation exemption for qualifying shareholdings; financing and cash deposit income may be exempt for certain collective undertakings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 621 (combined annual declaration for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax) submitted electronically via the Luxembourg tax administration's MyGuichet / eCDF portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory filing deadline is 31 May of the year following the tax year; automatic extension to 31 December of that same year applies when the return is filed through a Luxembourg-registered tax adviser.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification - legal name, registered office, Luxembourg business registration number (RCS), and unitary tax file number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company carrying on business through a Luxembourg permanent establishment must register with the RCS and identify the PE in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period and tax residency declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must state the PE's accounting period and attach a foreign tax residency certificate to support treaty protection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit before exemptions; reconciled from statutory commercial accounts to Luxembourg taxable basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only profits attributable to the Luxembourg PE are declared; transfer pricing adjustments must be made to reflect arm's length substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declared exemptions - participation exemption, IP regime income, and foreign branch profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must submit documentary evidence of qualifying holdings or IP rights; treaty exemption claims require Form 22 supporting details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and foreign withholding tax reclaims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident claimants must attach Form 22 and a completed foreign tax credit computation for income sourced in another jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative fine of up to €25,000, a surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax, and monthly delay interest of 0.5% on unpaid tax; fraudulent non-filing is criminally sanctionable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies; otherwise commonly reduced to 5% or 0% under applicable DTAs)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief, a Luxembourg-paying entity must obtain a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) of the foreign recipient, submit the Luxembourg withholding tax reclaim Form 22, and evidence the shareholding level and holding period; an advanced tax ruling from the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD) may be requested in advance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on outbound royalties or interest; under most DTAs the rate is 0% for both categories.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when aggregate controlled transactions exceed €1,000,000; Master File is required for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least €50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report is required when group revenue exceeds €750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies the Economic Substance Regulations through administrative circular LSC 2021 and EU ATAD/GAAR; a SARL must maintain real local office premises, qualified local employees, substantive commercial activity, and board decisions made in Luxembourg; thin capitalization restricts interest deductibility to 30% of EBITDA (leverage cap).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of taxable income, issuance of false invoices, or operation of an artificial shell arrangement to conceal profits from Luxembourg corporate taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to €250,000 or twice the evaded tax, additional interest of 6% per annum, and potential liability for personal wealth tax recalculations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or approve fraudulent filings may be jointly and severally liable for the evaded corporate tax; severance of the corporate veil leads to personal asset seizure, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Luxembourg SARL solely as a mailbox entity without locally steered economic activities, personnel, or business decision-making, including through an Amazon FBA commission flow stripped of substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of Luxembourg tax residence, denial of benefit of participation exemption, imposition of a 30% administrative penalty, and voidance under GAAR with reassessed taxes due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement a letterbox structure may incur personal civil restitution for the reclassified tax liability, travel restrictions, and disqualification from board functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or update the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners, concealing the underlying beneficial owner of the SARL, or routing Amazon FBA settlement proceeds through unregulated payment accounts to evade financial supervision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1,250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for money laundering under the Luxembourg Penal Code, plus administrative sanctions imposed by the CSSF; financial integrity lapses may lead to immediate bank account freezing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal conviction, confiscation of personal assets, travel bans while proceedings are pending, and aggravated liability if the corporation is deemed a mere instrument of criminal activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or maintain a contemporaneous Luxembourg Local File for intra-group services, royalties, or financing transactions when the €1,000,000 threshold is exceeded, or submitting inconsistent transactional documentation for the Amazon FBA business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to €10,000 for documentation non-compliance, upward adjustment of taxable profits by 10%, and potential loss of foreign tax credit; the tax authority may apply an arm's length re-determination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign misleading documentation may be held personally liable for penalties and civil damages; deliberate disregard of TP rules can be treated as fraudulent mismanagement leading to director disqualification and court-ordered compensation.
